Environmental Solutions Our comprehensive environmental solutions capabilities help customers safely manage their most technical waste streams. jobs.description: Overview Role Overview StoneX Financial Ltd. is seeking an experienced Director of Operational Risk to lead the operational risk agenda for the UK legal entity from our London office. Reporting to the Global Head of Enterprise Risk and SFL Head of Risk, this is a senior Second Line of Defense (2LOD) role responsible for the design, oversight and continuous improvement of the operational risk framework across the Firm’s regulated activities. The candidate will act as a trusted, self-directed risk leader who can independently own and discharge the entity’s local operational risk and regulatory obligations — including engagement with the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), compliance with the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA), and coordination with the National Futures Association (NFA) and other applicable authorities. A defining expectation of the role is the ability to escalate promptly and transparently to the Global Head of Enterprise Risk and the SFL Head of Risk (SMF4) at the earliest indication of any local risk concern, control weakness, incident or emerging regulatory matter. Responsibilities Key Responsibilities 2.1 Regulatory Oversight & Engagement Serve as the primary operational risk point of contact for UK and applicable overseas regulators, including the FCA and NFA, managing information requests, thematic reviews, and supervisory engagement independently and to a high professional standard. Own the entity’s compliance with the EU/UK Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA), including ICT risk management, digital operational resilience testing, ICT third-party risk oversight, and major ICT-related incident reporting obligations. Maintain current knowledge of the FCA Handbook (SYSC, SM&CR), operational resilience requirements (important business services, impact tolerances and mapping) and the MIFIDPRU / ICARA regime as it relates to operational risk. Interpret new and evolving regulations, assess entity impact, and translate requirements into practical, embedded controls and framework updates without requiring day-to-day direction. Prepare regulator-ready responses, attestations and submissions, ensuring language is accurate, proportionate and defensible. 2.2 Business-as-Usual (BAU) Operational Risk Management Independently manage the day-to-day operational risk activities of the UK entity, including Risk & Control Self-Assessments (RCSA), control monitoring plans, key risk indicators (KRIs) and risk appetite monitoring. Oversee the operational risk event / loss data capture process, ensuring timely recording, root-cause analysis, and remediation tracking to closure. Provide 2LOD challenge and oversight to First Line of Defense (1LOD) risk and control activities across front office, operations and support functions. Support operational risk scenario analysis and capital assessment inputs feeding the entity’s ICARA, including frequency and severity calibration where required. jobs.description: Amazon Security Lake is a fully managed security data lake service that automatically centralizes security data from AWS environments, SaaS providers, on-premises sources, and third-party products into a purpose-built data lake, normalizing it to the Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF) so customers get a single, analytics-ready view of their security posture across their entire organization. Security Lake operates across AWS commercial and GovCloud Regions and is trusted by many of the world's largest enterprises with their most sensitive data. We are looking for a Senior Software Development Engineer to serve as a technical leader for Security Lake and across the broader AWS Security Services organization. This role is unusual in its breadth: beyond owning the architecture and operational excellence of a security-critical, customer-facing data service, you will lead critical-path initiatives across our portfolio — including Amazon Security Hub and Amazon Inspector services. You will regularly be the senior engineer who lands in an unfamiliar codebase, earns the trust of another team's engineers, and converts an ambiguous business problem into a shipped, production system. If you want the reach of a platform role combined with the hands-on depth of a service team, this is that job. Key job responsibilities - Lead the design of major deliverables end-to-end — from working backwards on ambiguous requirements, through design documents and security reviews (threat models, AppSec, operational readiness), to implementation, launch, and production operation - Serve as a technical leader across AWS Security Services: embed with partner teams (Amazon Inspector, AWS Security Hub, AWS Config), deliver on their critical path to their standards and release calendars, and hand over cleanly with documentation, tests, canaries, and runbooks - Own and raise the operational bar for Security Lake: root-cause high-severity issues to resolution, harden APIs and canaries, drive down recurring alarms, and keep a security-critical service healthy and efficient - Set technical direction and simplify: promote re-use and extension over new components, pay down architectural debt, and turn one-off solutions into durable practices the whole team adopts - Drive decisions across team boundaries — when a dependency has no fix, propose the options, build consensus among stakeholders, and unblock the launch - Mentor and grow engineers through thorough (but kind) code and design reviews, onboarding of new team members, and raising the performance bar with every review A day in the life Most of your time is spent doing hands-on engineering: designing, writing, and reviewing code for distributed data-processing and control-plane systems (primarily Java and Python services with TypeScript/CDK infrastructure). In a typical week you might author a design for a new cross-service security capability and drive it through review with senior engineers from two other teams, ship code into a partner team's codebase, dig into a production alarm and turn the root cause into a fix plus a runbook, and give design feedback that changes the direction of a teammate's approach. You will share the team's on-call rotation and own customer issues to resolution — customers trust this service with their security data, and operational excellence is everyone's job, with senior engineers setting the example. The team is compact, senior-leaning, and geographically distributed, which means high autonomy, direct access to Principal Engineers and leadership across AWS Security Services, and visible ownership of everything you ship.
